title: JUmPER: Performance Data Monitoring, Instrumentation and Visualization for Jupyter Notebooks
problem: Performance analysis tools like Score-P exist but are difficult to integrate into Jupyter notebooks, requiring context switching and setup overhead. ML practitioners lack an accessible way to measure and visualize CPU and GPU utilization during interactive exploratory programming.
motivation: Computational performance optimization is critical for developing and deploying resource-efficient machine learning applications.
method: JUmPER creates a custom Jupyter kernel—the engine that runs code in notebooks—that collects CPU and GPU usage measurements while executing your code and displays them through special notebook commands. It integrates Score-P (a tool that identifies exactly where code spends its execution time) to provide detailed performance insights. To keep the notebook responsive, JUmPER passes data through RAM instead of disk (in-memory pipe communication) and efficiently converts Python's internal state in parallel, so measurement overhead stays minimal and doesn't interrupt your exploratory work.
key_novelty: A Jupyter-based kernel that combines low-overhead system monitoring, Score-P profiling, and interactive visualization for real-time performance analysis during coding.
contributions: JUmPER Jupyter kernel with integrated performance monitoring
Magic commands for interactive visualization of performance data
Score-P integration for fine-grained performance instrumentation
Low-overhead design through in-memory communication and parallel marshalling

metrics.other: kernel overhead reduction and performance visualization capabilities

primary_theme: Performance engineering infrastructure for Jupyter notebooks
